title: Rural Electrification Program
notebook: Forty thousand rural households lack reliable power. Children study by kerosene lamp.
Maric: thirty million ₭ over fourteen weeks. The Church runs most rural clinics and schools and wants power.
Midpoint at week seven: farming communities, Church facilities first, or a balanced rollout.

narrative.text: Forty thousand rural households in Thornfeld province and the eastern agricultural regions lack reliable electricity. Children do homework by kerosene lamp. Medical clinics cannot refrigerate vaccines. Farmers cannot operate modern equipment. The electrical grid stops at the provincial capitals and leaves the countryside in the last century. The Rural Electrification Program would extend power lines, build substations, and provide connection subsidies to connect every community of more than fifty households to the national grid.

Thirty million ₭, fourteen weeks. This is not glamorous — no one cuts ribbons for power lines. But electricity transforms rural life in ways that urban policymakers never fully appreciate. A refrigerator means food lasts longer. A light bulb means children can study after dark. A powered clinic means vaccines work. The Church runs most of the rural clinics and schools — they have been asking for electrification for years. If we do this, we should coordinate with them on prioritization.

The cost is significant but the program is structured so that connection fees from new customers eventually offset the infrastructure investment — not fully, but partially. The midpoint review at week seven will address the politically sensitive question of which communities get connected first. Farmers will argue for agricultural priority. The Church will argue for clinic and school priority. Both have legitimate claims.
This project has a midpoint decision at week seven on community prioritization — agricultural communities first, Church facilities first, or a balanced rollout.

choices.text: "Approve the electrification program. Thirty million ₭ from the infrastructure and welfare budgets. Maric, coordinate with the agricultural cooperatives and the Church parishes — I want every community above fifty households connected within eighteen months. This is the kind of government spending that pays dividends for generations. Light in every home. That is the promise."

"Defer the electrification program to the next budget cycle. Thirty million ₭ is substantial, and the Tyvaren border situation may require budget reallocation toward defense. If the security situation stabilizes, we will prioritize rural electrification in the next phase. The countryside has waited this long. They can wait a few more months."

"The government cannot subsidize electricity connections for every rural community. The electrical grid is a utility — it should be extended where it is economically viable, not where it is politically popular. Rural communities that want electricity can form cooperatives and fund their own connections. The state will provide technical assistance, not free infrastructure."
